title: Best Electric Blankets and Heated Throws UK
short: Under-blankets and heated throws compared by controls, timers, washability and running cost.
intro: Heating the person instead of the whole house can be far cheaper. Electric blankets warm the bed, and heated throws suit the sofa. This guide compares the models that UK testers rate highest, including their stated running costs.

guide.a: Electric blankets sit under the bottom sheet and warm the bed, often with dual controls for partners. Heated throws go over you on the sofa. Pick by where you will use it most.

guide.q: Are electric blankets safe to leave on overnight?
guide.a: Modern blankets have safety features such as auto shut-off and overheat protection, and many are designed for overnight use. Always follow the manufacturer's instructions, and check the product's safety information before leaving one on while you sleep.

guide.q: How much does an electric blanket cost to run?
guide.a: Mumsnet's estimates for the models here range from about 2p to 8p per hour, depending on wattage and your electricity tariff. That is often much less than heating a whole room.

guide.q: How do I look after an electric blanket?
guide.a: Check the label for washing instructions, since many are machine washable but not all. Store it flat or loosely rolled, avoid sharp folds, and replace it if it shows scorch marks, fraying or exposed wires, or once it passes the age the manufacturer recommends.
